summary: Peter Gyallay-Pap works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the London School of Economics and Political Science by 1990 and held an adjunct post at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2002–2015).
Peter Haskel specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson earned his PhD from Yale University (~1956–1961), where he taught from ~1961 to 1963. He later taught at Vassar College, the University of Washington, Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1973–1999).

Peter James Gilks specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and completed his PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers (attested 2010), alongside training under several traditional teachers.
Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He later held a position at SOAS University of London from circa 2002 to 2018.
Peter Koret works in Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held academic posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Rosemarie Lühr (~1990–1993). He held posts at the University of Giessen (~1995–2002), University of Düsseldorf (~2002–2004), and University of Göttingen (~2004).

Peter M. Scharf is a scholar of Indology, computational studies, and linguistics who earned his doctorate under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Brown University (2006–2009) and serves as President of The Sanskrit Library.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under doctoral supervisor Charles Keyes and teachers including Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

Peter N. Gregory specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning his PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi in 1981. He served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Kuroda Institute, and as Jill Ker Conway Professor at Smith College.
Peter Peterson was an Indologist. From circa 1873 to 1899, he served as a professor at the University of Mumbai and as Bombay Professor and Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College.

Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who earned his doctorate under Paul Hacker at Münster (~1970–1972) and completed his Habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who earned his doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Bonn under Dieter Schuh. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy, Humboldt University of Berlin, and was appointed to Bonn's chair of Tibetology in 2001.

Peter Skilling specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD from EPHE under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub by 2004. He founded and directed the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and held positions at EFEO, Chulalongkorn, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who completed his MA, MPhil, and PhD at Clare College, Cambridge (~1989–1998). He held posts at Reading, the Courtauld Institute, and Oxford, including the Classical Art Research Centre in 2011.

Peter Zieme is a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University (1960–1965). He worked at the GDR Academy of Sciences (1965–2007) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007).

Peter van der Veer is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Groningen and Utrecht. He held chairs at Amsterdam and Utrecht and was Director of the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity (~2007–2021).
